Job gains remain solid and unemployment low, but below-target inflation, low market-based inflation compensation, and ongoing weakness in business fixed investment and exports point to demand-side softness; in line with McCallum and Nelson (1999) and Taylor-type rules, the 25 bp cut supports stabilizing output and inflation, while the expectations channel (Cagan, 1956; Galí, Gertler, and López-Salido) helps explain muted price pressures despite a tight labor market; given investment’s central role in business-cycle fluctuations and real GDP in the literature, the overall tone is cautiously positive rather than outright strong.
